headline: Siyaram Silk Mills Limited: Allotment of Preference Shares as Bonus pursuant to Scheme of Arrangement/Amalgamation
sum: Siyaram Silk Mills allotted 181.48 crore Series I and 136.11 crore Series II preference shares as bonus under a scheme of arrangement/amalgamation. The allotment was approved at the company's board meeting on 25 August 2026.
implication: Bonus allotment of preference shares under a reverse triangular merger or consolidation structure signals tax-neutral capital reorganisation and potential minority protection via preference terms; practitioners should verify the scheme's status under NCLT and the ranking/redemption features of each series.
detail: Siyaram Silk Mills Limited, a textile and luxury fabric manufacturer listed on NSE, allotted a total of 317.59 crore preference shares in two tranches (Series I: 181.48 crore; Series II: 136.11 crore) as bonus securities to shareholders pursuant to a scheme of arrangement or amalgamation. The allotment was formally notified to NSE on 25 August 2026 following board approval. The scheme structure suggests a potential group consolidation, reorganisation or merger affecting the capital base. Preference share issuance as bonus (rather than cash or equity) typically preserves liquidity and signals a restructuring gating item requiring NCLT sanction.

framework.note: central: Scheme of Arrangement requires NCLT approval; merger, amalgamation, and capital reorganisation all gated here.
central: Issuance of bonus securities (preference or equity) must comply with bonus capitalisation rules and board/shareholder approval.
central: Rights, preferences, redemption, and redemption premium of preference shares must be defined and registered; cumulative vs. non-cumulative, voting rights.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015, Reg. 30, Schedule III
framework.note: central: Mandatory disclosure of material corporate action (scheme sanction, allotment, bonus, preference issue) to stock exchange and public within prescribed timelines.

framework.ref: Income Tax Act 1961, s. 115O (now s. 115BAA for corporates); s. 47(vi) (scheme mergers)
framework.note: amended: Bonus allotment and scheme mergers attract specific tax treatment; recent amendments to corporate tax rates and surcharges require review.

framework.ref: RBI Prudential Norms (if banking/NBFC entity involved)
framework.note: May apply if any scheme party is a financial services entity; not clearly indicated here.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, s. 230A (if cross-default or distressed scenario)
framework.note: If scheme follows IBC resolution plan or involves distressed entity, this gate applies; otherwise dormant.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act 1999, s. 6 (if cross-border element)
framework.note: If scheme involves NRI/FPI holders or overseas parent, FDI/repatriation rules apply.

structure.consideration: 181,480,352 Series I Preference Shares + 136,110,264 Series II Preference Shares (total ~317.59 crore shares); allotted as bonus, no cash consideration disclosed.
conditions: NCLT sanction of Scheme of Arrangement/Amalgamation (inferred as mandatory pre-condition)
Preference share terms (redemption price, cumulative/non-cumulative status, dividend, voting) to be confirmed from scheme document
approvals: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) sanction of Scheme (status not stated in available disclosure)
Stock Exchange (NSE) notification and listing approval
structure.novel: Issuance of two distinct series of preference shares (Series I and II) with significantly different volumes (181.48 cr vs. 136.11 cr) suggests differentiated shareholder classes or staged reorganisation; the 4:3 ratio and dual-series structure may indicate merging entities or subsidiary upsizing.

triggers.note: Scheme of Arrangement gating: NCLT sanction is the master trigger for entire reorganisation.
Disclosure obligation: company must file material update (allotment intimation) to exchange and publish on website within 24 hours of allotment.
Bonus share issuance: board and shareholder approval, capitalisation of reserves, no fresh consideration.
Tax-neutral treatment of scheme mergers; bonus allotment may qualify for exemption depending on scheme classification (merger vs. reconstruction).
